audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer attributes Karma's root to the wrong ability, six times. early says 'that zone roots you if you sit in it'; mid says 'blink out of the detonation circle before it roots you'; whys[4] says 'her Soulflare root'; whys[5] says 'the Soulflare root'; wants.foe[1] says 'Land empowered Soulflare (Mantra Q) to root you in the zone'; spikes[3] says to blink in 'after dodging Soulflare'. Mantra Q creates a delayed damage cataclysm and slows - it has no root. The root is Focused Resolve, her W, which the content layer never mentions once. Meanwhile the FULL layer correctly names Focused Resolve as the matchup-defining cooldown, so the two layers are describing different abilities.
audit.why: A reader who sidesteps the Soulflare circle and then stands still at 700 units has done exactly the wrong thing, because the root that actually catches them is a targeted tether they are already inside. And the counterplay the page needs is a perfect fit for this champion and appears nowhere: Focused Resolve roots only IF THE TETHER IS NOT BROKEN, it reaches 675 units, and Riftwalk is a 500-unit blink on a 5/3.5/2 second cooldown. Blinking directly away breaks the tether and cancels the root before it lands. That is the single best use of Kassadin's ultimate in this matchup and neither layer says it. Second omission: Gathering Fire means every damaging ability she lands shortens Mantra, so denying her poke targets is what keeps her ultimate down.
audit.corrected: Root reattributed to Focused Resolve in all six places, with the 675-range tether and the Riftwalk break written in; Gathering Fire's Mantra reduction added; Soulflare left as what it is, a delayed damage zone.
sources: champ-data/_kits/karma.json (W Focused Resolve: 'creates a tether... If the tether is not broken, the enemy will be rooted', range 675, cooldown 12; Q Mantra Bonus: 'creating a cataclysm which deals damage after a short delay'; P Gathering Fire: 'damaging abilities will reduce the cooldown of Mantra')

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one cooldown appears in either layer, and Mantra's availability at level 1 is never mentioned despite the page treating the empowered cast as a mid-game threat.
audit.why: Mantra is available at level 1 and costs no skill point, so the empowered cast exists in the very first wave - the page's Lvl 2-3 spike is already late. Mantra is 40/38/36/34s and Gathering Fire shortens it every time she lands damage. Focused Resolve is a flat 12s. Inner Flame is 9/8/7/6/5s at 950 range against your 650. Inspire is 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s. Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2s, which is what beats a 12-second tether.
audit.corrected: Mantra's level-1 availability and 40s, Focused Resolve's 12s, Inner Flame's 9s and the 950-vs-650 range gap written into the spikes, early and the cooldown block.
sources: champ-data/_kits/karma.json (R: 'Mantra is available at level 1 and does not require a skill point')

audit.whatIsWrong: full.tldr is boilerplate shared with other matchups - 'If his damage is magic, your Q eats it - if it's physical, this is a real lane' - and it also calls Karma 'his'.
audit.why: Karma deals magic damage across her entire kit, so the conditional resolves. Void Stone reduces incoming magic and Null Sphere's shield absorbs magic, which makes both of Kassadin's defensive tools live in this lane - an unstated structural advantage that a hedged tldr throws away, and the real reason a 650-range melee mage survives a 950-range poke lane at all.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to the resolved case in the right pronoun: her damage is all magic, both your tools bite, and range rather than damage is the problem.

notes: WRONG ABILITY, six places, and the two layers disagreed with each other. The content layer repeatedly credits a ROOT to Soulflare (Mantra Q) - 'that zone roots you if you sit in it', 'blink out of the detonation circle before it roots you', 'her Soulflare root', and three more. Mantra Q creates a delayed damage cataclysm and slows; it does not root. The root is Focused Resolve, her W, which the content layer never names once - while the full layer correctly calls Focused Resolve the matchup-defining cooldown. A reader dodging the Soulflare circle and then standing still is doing precisely the wrong thing. THE COUNTERPLAY THAT WAS MISSING is a near-perfect fit for this champion and appears in neither layer: Focused Resolve roots only IF THE TETHER IS NOT BROKEN, it reaches 675 units, and Riftwalk is a 500-unit blink on 5/3.5/2s - blinking straight away from her breaks the tether and cancels the root. Also added: Mantra needs no skill point and is available at LEVEL 1, so the empowered cast exists in the first wave, and Gathering Fire shortens its 40 seconds every time she lands damage, which makes denying her poke targets a way to keep her ultimate down. Cooldowns added throughout (Focused Resolve flat 12s, Mantra 40/38/36/34s, Inner Flame 9/8/7/6/5s, the 950-vs-650 range gap). full.tldr was the generic if-magic/if-physical boilerplate and called Karma 'his'; her kit is magic end to end, which makes Void Stone and the Q shield both live and is the real reason this lane is survivable. Fixed: breakdown.late called Null Sphere a silence. LEVEL CHART: the packet's defect note ('chart gives Karma 6/7 stages vs 1') is STALE - the stored chart already reads Karma x4, Skill, Skill, Kassadin and both layers agree. I left it alone. Worth your eye though: 67.31% over 52 games is a big win rate for a chart in which Kassadin owns one stage, and First item reads Skill while whys[5] says 'she keeps the edge'. Moving it would mean overwriting text that argues against the move, so I did not.
